technical_principles.summary: Kickboxing S&C should support repeated explosive strikes, footwork, guard endurance, trunk rotation, hip mobility, calf/ankle stiffness, adductor capacity, and recovery between rounds.
Sparring, low-kick contact, bag impact, pad impact, and head contact are training loads and should be progressed like running volume or lifting volume.
Competition week should reduce soreness, hard sparring, heavy eccentric work, and novelty while preserving speed, timing, tactical confidence, and weight/recovery stability.

sport_training_rules.rule: Progress contact load gradually across bag, pad, partner, sparring, low-kick, and head-contact exposure. Do not treat contact as free conditioning volume.
recommended_action: Separate technical, conditioning, and contact stress.
Track pain, headache, wrist/hand symptoms, shin/ankle soreness, and sleep/readiness after contact days.
blocked_action: heavy bag power volume with wrist pain

sport_training_rules.rule: Head-contact sparring should be conservative, supervised, and removed when concussion-like symptoms, headaches, dizziness, visual symptoms, or unusual fatigue occur.
recommended_action: Prefer technical sparring, body-only rounds, and pad constraints for beginners.
Use medical/coach review for head-contact symptoms.
blocked_action: hard head sparring for fitness users

sport_training_rules.rule: Low-kick, checking, bouncing footwork, and kicking volume should be adjusted for shin, ankle, knee, hip, adductor, and low-back symptoms.
recommended_action: Use technical drills, calf/soleus, adductor, hip-control, and ankle-foot capacity work.
Limit high-impact conditioning and hard low-kick exchanges when symptoms rise.
blocked_action: hard low-kick sparring with knee or shin pain

planning_rules.rule: Avoid stacking hard sparring, heavy lower-body strength, high-volume kicking, and intense conditioning on consecutive days unless the athlete is advanced and recovering well.
recommended_action: Place strength and power to support technical sessions, not destroy them.
Use aerobic and mobility work on recovery days.
blocked_action: hard sparring day after heavy eccentric legs for beginners
low-kick sparring after shin pain spike

planning_rules.rule: Competition week should drop hard sparring, soreness-producing lifting, hard low-kick contact, and new techniques while preserving speed, timing, tactical rehearsal, mobility, and confidence.
recommended_action: Use short pad rounds, footwork, defensive sharpness, light power primers, and recovery.
Keep weight-making and hydration stress conservative.

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Progress from no-contact technical skill to controlled contact safely.
progression_steps: Partner feeds with no return fire.
Technical defense drills with light contact.
Light technical sparring with coach constraints.
progression_signals: keeps eyes open and guard under contact

sport_skill_assessments.summary: Assess whether the athlete can safely receive and manage controlled contact.
metrics: guard and stance under partner feed
